toolfolder.problem: is installed in {folder}, but that folder is not on PATH
toolfolder.option.smith.label: Let smith use it from that folder (recommended)
toolfolder.option.smith.hint: smith adds {folder} to PATH for its own tasks, checks and plugins, and records it in {file}; your PATH stays as it is
toolfolder.option.userpath.label: Add the folder to your user PATH
toolfolder.option.userpath.hint: after you confirm, smith adds {folder} to the Path of your Windows user (not the machine); open a new terminal after
toolfolder.option.show.label: Show me the folder and change nothing
toolfolder.option.show.hint: smith prints the folder and the command that adds it to your PATH
toolfolder.used:
smith now uses {title} from {folder}. Your PATH did not change.
→ Run smith tools to check.
toolfolder.userpath.question: smith will add {folder} to the Path of your Windows user. Terminals that are open now do not see it.
toolfolder.userpath.yes.hint: smith runs the command in PowerShell; open a new terminal after
toolfolder.userpath.no.hint: smith prints the command so you can run it later
toolfolder.userpath.done:
{folder} is on your user PATH now.
→ Open a new terminal: terminals that are already open do not see the change.
toolfolder.userpath.failed:
smith could not change your PATH: {reason}
→ Run this in PowerShell yourself: {command}
toolfolder.found.after: winget put {title} in {folder}, but that folder is not on PATH.
toolfolder.already: winget says {title} is already installed and has no newer version.
toolfolder.use.unknown: smith does not know a tool named {tool}
toolfolder.use.unknown.remedy: smith tools lists the tools of this workspace
toolfolder.use.none: smith found no folder that holds {program} where winget puts its packages
toolfolder.use.none.remedy: install it first: smith tools install {tool}
toolfolder.use.short: Let smith use a tool from the folder winget put it in, without a change to PATH
